Subject: PrivGPU traffic classification and headroom matrix

Ian —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per request, I attached an initial headroom matrix and a simple network topology sketch to help us converge on capacity targets for your private GPU pool. This note summarizes our assumptions and the specific inputs we need from Graystone to finalize sizing.

High-level ask: please confirm the traffic mix and the two SLA targets below so we can produce a conservative and an aggressive capacity plan.

Assumptions included in the attached spreadsheet (headroom-matrix-v1.xlsx):
- Model mix: 60% chat (avg prompt+response tokens 350), 30% single-shot generation (avg 120 tokens), 10% embeddings/rerank.
- Target p50 latency requirement for chat: 200ms token-tail (application-level SLO: 95th request < 600ms).
- Concurrent active sessions: baseline 120, peak 900 (10x burst window 3–5 mins).
- Typical batch sizes: 1–4 for chat, 8–16 for bulk embeddings.
- Network egress cap: 10 Gbps per rack; prefer design that tolerates one link at 70% utilization without impacting latency.

Questions for Graystone (please reply inline):
1) Confirm expected sustained QPS (reqs/sec) for the 8am–6pm window and expected peak factor.
2) Any hard egress/ingress caps on the VPC side (do you want us to assume 10Gbps or 25Gbps?).
3) Are there multiple regional pools or single-site deployment? (affects cross-region fallback policy)
4) Would you accept a warm-pool strategy (reserved VMs GPU warm, instant admission) or prefer cold scale with a slightly higher headroom reserve?

Operational notes we recommend:
- Admission control tiers (gold/silver/bulk) mapped to latency budgets and model quantization profiles.
- KV cache warmup and prefix caching for large chat families to reduce per-token compute during bursts.
- A 20–30% headroom cushion for ephemeral model hot-starts during canary deploys.

Next steps: if the numbers below look right, I’ll have Laura and Marissa run two scenarios (conservative 2.5x headroom, aggressive 1.6x) and share updated attachments by Thursday. Also included a suggested 30m alignment slot (calendly link).

Attachments: headroom-matrix-v1.xlsx (summary + calc tabs), network-topology-proposal.png

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the attachments. A few answers inline below and one clarifying ask.

1) Sustained QPS: baseline ~75 req/s across the day, with scheduled analytics bursts that can push to ~850 req/s for 4–6 minutes (we run a nightly ingest that also spikes at 2am).
2) Network caps: Our infra team is currently allocating 25Gbps to the VPC egress; however, we prefer not to exceed 18Gbps sustained per rack.
3) Deployment: single-site (primary data center in us-east-1) with a DR site in us-west-2 that should be manual-failover for now.
4) Warm pool: yes — we prefer warm-pool for customer-facing latency-sensitive traffic, but we want a fallback cold-scale option for cost control.

A clarifying ask: during the 4–6 minute bursts we typically have a shift in model mix toward more short single-shot generations (up to 50% of requests). Can your headroom matrix show the difference if short generations dominate during burst windows?

Also looping in our infra lead, Melissa (listed on the attached network review); she may follow up with topology constraints.

Thanks Ian — this is helpful. I ran a compact scenario in the sheet and summarized three candidate sizing profiles (all numbers are illustrative; see tab "summary").

Summary (short):
- Conservative: assume burst model mix flips to 50% short gens + 50% chat; reserve 2.5x of baseline GPU capacity; recommend 8 nodes (A100 equivalent) w/ 25Gbps per rack and 30% warm pool sized for hot sessions.
- Balanced: reserve 1.8x baseline; recommend 6 nodes; warm pool 20%; admission-control gold lane for latency-sensitive chat (p50 target ~180ms).
- Lean (cost-optimized): reserve 1.4x baseline, 5 nodes, warm pool 10%, heavier batching on short genera tions — will increase p95 slightly during spikes.

Key network notes:
- With 25Gbps egress allocation and 18Gbps sustained preference, we route burst-heavy traffic to prioritized cross-connects and rely on dynamic throttling on bulk lanes.
- KV cache warmup is essential: if you can pre-warm the top 50 prefixes, we reduce compute per-token by ~15–22% during spikes.

Operational tradeoffs to consider:
- Warm pool size reduces tail latency but increases commit costs.
- Admission-control policies can protect latency SLAs by shedding noncritical traffic to bulk lanes during short spikes.
- If Graystone wants to cap spend strictly, prefer the Lean profile + scheduled pre-warm for known nightly spikes.

I attached an updated summary view in the same spreadsheet and annotated the topology png with suggested cross-connect lanes. If this looks good, Marissa will produce a final technical handoff doc and a runbook for DR and canary deployments.
